newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria April inflation seen down to 4-5 pct m/m.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria April inflation seen down to 4-5 pct m/m.

text.p: Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation is expected to slow down to around four to five percent in April from 12.3 percent in March and 243 percent in February, a National Statistics Institute (NSI) official said.

"We expect monthly inflation to slow down to some four to five percent this month due to the lev rise and the lack of considerable changes in the prices of basic goods," a NSI official who declined to be named, told Reuters.
A rise of energy prices in line with pledges made to multilateral lenders was seen as the main factor for April inflation, said the official.
Prices of 32 most traded foods monitored by the government fell 0.3 percent between April 10 and April 21 after falling 2.4 percent in the first ten days of this month, the official said.
The lev rose to 1,500 per dollar on April 21 from around 1,600 on April 1 on the local interbank market. It traded near 1,780 at the beginning of March.
A fall in fuel prices by eight to nine percent from April 1 were also a reason for monthly inflation to slow down, said the official.
A one-digit monthly inflation was also expected in May if the lev/dollar exchange rate was stable, said the official.
Monthly inflation slowed to 12.3 percent last month from peaking at 242.7 percent in February as the interim cabinet took office and launched urgent stabilisation measures.

The cabinet raised electricity prices by an average of 30 percent and central heating prices by 70 percent from April 1 to match production costs to the sharp lev fall in January and February. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
